clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was discriminated against on grounds of political opinion in violation of Article 12(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner alleged that his arrest and detention were mala fide and motivated by his political affiliation opposing the ruling party, constituting discrimination under Article 12(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents denied mala fide intent and justified the arrest and detention based on reasonable suspicion and lawful authority under Emergency Regulations.
key_facts: Petitioner was a former Member of Parliament and belonged to an opposition political party.
Petitioner was arrested and detained under Emergency Regulations related to investigation of a court arson.
Petitioner alleged mala fide questioning and detention due to political reasons.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court found the material insufficient to establish discrimination on political grounds under Article 12(2).
reasoning.application_to_facts: Despite the petitioner’s allegations, the Court noted lack of substantive evidence or submissions proving discriminatory intent or treatment based on political opinion.
principles_established: Allegations of discrimination under Article 12(2) require supporting material or evidence.
Mala fide intent must be substantiated to prove discrimination.

outcome.holding: The petitioner's claim under Article 12(2) was dismissed due to insufficient material to prove discrimination.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The petitioner’s claim of discrimination on political grounds was central to his fundamental rights complaint, but the Court found no sufficient evidence to uphold it.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court held that the material set out in the petition was insufficient to establish the claim under Article 12(2) and dismissed the claim accordingly.
